directive:
The Stage-0 counterexample is valid under the frozen primitives: candidate attractors need not be distinct and J need not be determined by the limiting state, so identical attractors with a terminal-score-sign label can satisfy attraction while violating stable convergence relative to sigma(J). Author and prove a complete, atomic, faithful correction; do not restore label stability and do not add an assumption that forces J to be recoverable from the state.

Replace the headline Theorem 1 claim by the strongest label-free result actually implied by the primitives. Formulate the uniform finite-T CDF approximation using explicitly P-specific `mathcal J_P`, `p_{P,j}`, and `V_{P,j}` and exactly one `sup_{||c||_2=1}` quantifier (no shadowing outer `for every c`). State the approximation to the P-specific finite centered Gaussian mixture before taking limits. When discussing limiting laws, quantify an explicit sequence or subsequence along which the finite mixture parameters converge; do not assert an unqualified full-sequence fixed mixture if the parameters may vary with T and P. Preserve the valid predictable-QV bound, exact-root localization, linearization, and the conclusion that unequal positive-mass projected variances yield a non-Gaussian centered Gaussian mixture along such a convergent sequence/subsequence.

Synchronize Theorem 3's every-level deterministic-sandwich iff and Theorem 4's all-contrast/matrixwise iff with that sequence/subsequence formulation. State precisely which P-specific positive-mass support and limiting mixture parameters the iff ranges over, and retain the equality-of-laws argument. Update Proposition 1's in-class separation witness and all exposition/sanity-reduction text so they instantiate the corrected label-free/subsequential statements without claiming stable convergence. Recheck whether `def:stable-limit-criterion` remains needed; remove or rewrite it as a non-load-bearing comparison definition if the corrected theorem no longer uses it.

Synchronize all prose and metadata with the corrected headline: `tldr`, `project_justification.{gap,niche,fill}`, `related_work`, `honest_scope`, novelty justification, theorem justification/gap/consumer fields, comparator table, limitations, summaries, and dependency/free-symbol carriers must stop saying the paper proves basin-label-stable or basin-measurable stable convergence. Lead with what is proved: uniform P-specific finite-mixture approximation, feasible same-path realized-QV pivotality, and exact deterministic-sandwich boundaries. Preserve the achieved conditional field-tier positioning and the already-adjudicated Saco dependency correction for Theorem 2. Re-prove every affected node against the single coherent postimage, and do not alter the dynamics-only Guo-Xu open question in this round.

changed.from: For the common envelopes defining \(\mathfrak P_T\), the existing derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply the nonprimitive upper bounds \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P[\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\|_{\mathrm{op}}]\le C(r_T+\delta_T)\). The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, and bounded-IPW martingale concentration gives \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply by a quantitative inverse-function argument that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it lies at distance \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it belongs to \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), \(G_T(\widehat\theta_T)=0\) on \(E_T\), and the fallback \(\widehat\theta_T=\widetilde\theta_T\) occurs only on a uniformly negligible event. With \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), the exact-root linearization is \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)\), and \((\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*),J,T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T)\) converges stably relative to \(\sigma(J)\) to \((-V_J^{1/2}Z,J,\Omega_J)\). If \(c^\top V_jc\) differs across two positive-mass basins, the unconditional limit of \(c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\) is a non-Gaussian centered normal scale mixture.
changed.to:
For each \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), write \(\mathcal J_P=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), \(p_{P,j}=P(J=j)\), and let \(V_{P,j}\) denote the value of \(V_j\) under \(P\). The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_P\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest label-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is the \(P\)-specific finite-mixture approximation
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), there is a subsequence \(T_\ell\to\infty\), a fixed set \(\mathcal J_0\), and limits \(p_j^\infty\) and positive-definite \(V_j^\infty\) such that \(\mathcal J_{P_{T_\ell}}=\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Along this subsequence, every fixed contrast has the centered Gaussian-mixture limit with weights \(p_j^\infty\) and projected variances \(c^\top V_j^\infty c\), omitting zero limiting weights. If two positive limiting weights have unequal projected variances, this limit is not Gaussian. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(J)\), even when all basin covariance matrices are equal.
changed.reason: The frozen assumptions permit identical attractors and a label J chosen from terminal score information, so they do not imply stable convergence relative to sigma(J). The corrected claim retains every valid localization and QV conclusion and replaces the false joint limit by the strongest uniformly provable P-specific marginal mixture approximation, with explicit convergent subsequences.

changed.from: Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic \(\Sigma\). Under the stable limit in Theorem 1 with \(p_j>0\), \(\lim_{T\to\infty}P\{\tau\in C_T^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) if and only if \(c^\top V_jc=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). The necessity is an equality-of-laws result for the finite centered Gaussian scale mixture, not a variance-matching argument at one nominal level.
changed.to:
Let \(T_\ell\to\infty\) and \(P_\ell\in\mathfrak P_{T_\ell}\) be a sequence or subsequence for which the \(P_\ell\)-specific mixture parameters in Theorem 1 have a fixed support \(\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_\ell,j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_\ell,j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Put \(\mathcal J_\infty=\{j\in\mathcal J_0:p_j^\infty>0\}\). Fix nonzero \(c\) and deterministic positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Then
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}P_\ell\{\tau\in C_{T_\ell}^{\Sigma}(c,\alpha)\}=1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }\alpha\in(0,1)
\]
if and only if \(c^\top V_j^\infty c=c^\top\Sigma c\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). The necessity identifies the law of the limiting finite centered Gaussian scale mixture from coverage at every nominal level; it is not a one-level variance-matching claim.
changed.reason: Without fixed full-sequence mixture parameters, the every-level iff is meaningful along a sequence or subsequence on which the P-specific weights and covariance matrices converge. Zero limiting weights must be excluded from the necessity conclusion.

changed.from: A single deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\). Equivalently, \(V_J\) is almost surely deterministic. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.
changed.to: Along any sequence or subsequence with limiting mixture parameters \((p_j^\infty,V_j^\infty)_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}\) as in Theorem 3, a single deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). Equivalently, the limiting selected covariance that equals \(V_j^\infty\) with probability \(p_j^\infty\) is almost surely the deterministic matrix \(\Sigma\). In the fixed-parameter special case this is equivalent to \(V_J=\Sigma\) almost surely. The implication from all projected equalities to matrix equality follows by polarization.
changed.reason: The matrixwise boundary must refer to the positive-weight limiting covariance atoms of the same convergent sequence or subsequence as the corrected contrastwise theorem, rather than an unqualified full-sequence random matrix.

directive:
D0-SOLVE only `oeq:guoxu-finite-attractor-certification`; preserve every settled inference theorem and do not turn finite selection, separatrix avoidance, or a uniform attraction modulus into an assumption. Retain the already proved partial classification: q_{t,a}=O(1/t) a.s.; on L_+ and L_- the slope limits are respectively (19/46,-79/3804) and (-79/634,19/276); each separated regime has positive probability from every allowed initialization; and any common-coordinate subsequential limit must satisfy the occupation equation already derived in (13), with the candidate (u,b)=((47+sqrt(4609))/150,(sqrt(4609)-91)/1224) under the two-regime occupation relation. Do not spend another round re-deriving those facts.

First repair the node's local well-posedness without changing its subject: Guo--Xu sec. 3.1 specifies only Gaussian noise, not armwise numerical variances. State the bounded analogue for arbitrary fixed explicit sigma_1,sigma_2>0 (and an explicit deterministic tie arm), or choose and declare concrete values; do not say they are published Guo--Xu variances.

Then pursue the simplest standard remaining construction in normalized sufficient-statistic state, not in slopes alone. For t>=1 set Psi_t=(D_{t,1}/t,D_{t,2}/t,N_{t,1}/t,N_{t,2}/t), write beta_a=N_a/D_a, derive the exact 1/(t+1) stochastic-approximation recursion, and show its interpolation is a bounded perturbed solution of the upper-semicontinuous convexified differential inclusion whose drift is h_+-Psi when beta_1>beta_2, h_--Psi when beta_1<beta_2, and co{h_+-Psi,h_--Psi} on beta_1=beta_2. Account explicitly for the vanishing UCB bonus O(t^-1/2) and the bounded martingale error. Use Benaim--Hofbauer--Sorin 2005, Hypothesis 1.1, Theorems 3.6 and 4.2, and Proposition 3.27--not a smooth ODE asserted for the slope projection--to classify every internally chain-transitive set of this piecewise-affine inclusion.

Strongest determinate target for this round: prove that every projected a.s. limit set is a singleton among beta_+, beta_-, and the explicitly derived switching-state candidate (b,b), or else exhibit and characterize the additional ICT set that prevents this three-candidate theorem. This closes the global limit-set classification as far as the standard differential-inclusion literature honestly permits and yields pathwise Cesaro convergence to the selected candidate. Only after that classification, separately test whether the switching candidate is a normally repulsive equilibrium in a genuinely smooth local reduction and verify all of Pemantle 1990 Theorem 1 conditions (p.700), especially C^2 drift and one-sided omnidirectional noise. If those hypotheses cannot be proved because the drift remains discontinuous, leave P{limit=(b,b)}=0 as the narrowed open question; do not cite Pemantle as a turnkey exclusion and do not upgrade to P(L_+ union L_-)=1.

Do not assert deterministic r_T(K_0),delta_T(K_0) uniform over compact initial sets from pointwise convergence or a finite-cover sentence. Such uniformity requires a separate quantitative hitting/escape estimate and continuity/equicontinuity that the hard argmax kernel does not supply. If no such estimate is proved, record only pointwise Cesaro convergence for each fixed initialization/candidate and leave compact-uniform moduli open. Borkar 2002 may support local positive-probability lock-in only after entry into an attraction domain; it may not be used to prove global entry because its result presupposes finitely many candidate limits. Preserve the dynamics-only scope: no claim of membership in P_T and no application of Theorems 1--2.

Exact source locators: Guo--Xu, arXiv:2606.22639v1, sec. 3.1, HTML lines 337--355 and source `Sections/Sec3_Inference_Guarantee.tex` lines 201--213; Borkar, DOI 10.1017/S0963548301004953, publisher abstract and pp.11--20; Pemantle, Ann. Probab. 18 (1990), Theorem 1 on p.700 (conditions (i)--(iv)); Benaim--Hofbauer--Sorin, DOI 10.1137/S0363012904439301, Hypothesis 1.1 p.329, Theorem 3.6 p.337, Proposition 3.27 pp.341--342, Theorem 4.2 p.343.

Do not re-suggest: slope-only Markov/ODE analysis; treating K_GX=[-1,1]^2 as an invariant augmented state space; Borkar as global basin entry; Pemantle without a C^2 local drift; finite-cover uniformization from pointwise convergence; unspecified "published Gaussian variances"; or any inference/class-membership conclusion.

For each \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\), write \(\mathcal J_P=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), \(p_{P,j}=P(J=j)\), and let \(V_{P,j}\) denote the value of \(V_j\) under \(P\). The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\) and \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_P\). There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest label-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is the \(P\)-specific finite-mixture approximation
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_P}p_{P,j}\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_{P,j}c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), there is a subsequence \(T_\ell\to\infty\), a fixed set \(\mathcal J_0\), and limits \(p_j^\infty\) and positive-definite \(V_j^\infty\) such that \(\mathcal J_{P_{T_\ell}}=\mathcal J_0\), \(p_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to p_j^\infty\), and \(V_{P_{T_\ell},j}\to V_j^\infty\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\). Along this subsequence, every fixed contrast has the centered Gaussian-mixture limit with weights \(p_j^\infty\) and projected variances \(c^\top V_j^\infty c\), omitting zero limiting weights. If two positive limiting weights have unequal projected variances, this limit is not Gaussian. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(J)\), even when all basin covariance matrices are equal.

Using the exact-root linearization on \(E_T\) and carrying its uniformly negligible fallback event \(E_T^c\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_T\),
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad

\]

\[

 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.

\[

if and only if

changed.from: Along any sequence or subsequence with limiting mixture parameters \((p_j^\infty,V_j^\infty)_{j\in\mathcal J_\infty}\) as in Theorem 3, a single deterministic positive-definite matrix \(\Sigma\) gives asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every nonzero contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(V_j^\infty=\Sigma\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_\infty\). The fixed states obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}attractor\text{-}separation}\), the terminal label and selected state obey \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), every label obeys \(\mathrm{ass:basin\text{-}mass\text{-}floor}\), and the path approximation is supplied solely by \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}attraction\text{-}modulus}\). Thus \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\), every one of the \(m\) separated basins has mass at least \(p_-\), and the policy path is approximated by its selected attractor only through the uniform Cesaro inequality. Pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is not imposed.

edit.reason: Restore the finite-tail-attractor class and include the three atomic carriers for separation, terminal selection, and positive basin mass.

changed.from:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_\infty\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[\left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_\infty\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly. The strongest terminal-representative-free distributional conclusion implied by these primitives is
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}
 -E_P\Phi\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_\infty c}}\right)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_\infty
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_\infty\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. In general, the class primitives do not imply stable convergence relative to \(\sigma(\eta_\infty)\), even when \(V_\infty\) is deterministic.
changed.to:
The common derivative and bounded-IPW envelopes imply
\[
 \|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1,
 \qquad
 \omega_-I_d\preceq\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}.
\]
The finite-tail-selection relation gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely. There is a finite constant \(C\), independent of \(T\) and \(P\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}E_P\!\left[
 \left\|T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T-\Omega_J\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\right]
 \le C(r_T+\delta_T).
\]
The preliminary estimator is uniformly consistent, \(G_T(\theta^*)=O_P(T^{-1/2})\), and \(\partial_\theta G_T(\theta^*)-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})\) uniformly. Together with \(D_2\rho/\varepsilon<h_-/4\), these bounds imply that, with probability tending uniformly to one, there is a unique empirical root in the closed \(\rho\)-ball about \(\theta^*\), it is \(O_P(T^{-1/2})\) from \(\theta^*\), and it is the unique member of \(\mathcal Z_T\). Hence \(\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}P(E_T^c)\to0\), and
\[
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(e_T)
\]
uniformly.

For every basin \(j\in\mathcal J\), the basin-conditional Gaussian approximation is uniform:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\!\left\{c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\mid J=j\right\}
 -\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
More strongly, the corresponding joint \(\sigma(J)\)-stable Gaussian kernel is expressed by
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \sup_{\psi:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to[-1,1]}
 \left|E_P\!\left[\psi(J)\mathbf1\!\left\{
 c^\top\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)\le z\right\}\right]
 -\sum_{j=1}^mp_j\psi(j)\Phi\!\left(\frac{z}{\sqrt{c^\top V_jc}}\right)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\omega_-}{(KD_1)^2}I_d\preceq V_j
 \preceq\frac{KB^2}{\varepsilon h_-^2}I_d
 \quad\text{for every }j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Thus, for every sequence \(P_T\in\mathfrak P_T\), the laws of \(V_J\) have a weakly convergent subsequence with a limiting law \(\mu\) supported on the displayed compact covariance set. Along that subsequence, every fixed nonzero contrast has the centered Gaussian scale-mixture limit \(\sqrt{c^\top Vc}\,Z_1\), where \(V\sim\mu\), \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\), and \(V\) and \(Z_1\) are independent. This limit is Gaussian if and only if \(c^\top Vc\) is \(\mu\)-almost surely constant. No pointwise convergence of \(\eta_t\) is used.
changed.reason: The supplied class correction narrows the law class from an arbitrary terminal representative to finitely many uniformly separated positive-mass attractors. That restriction makes the terminal label recoverable from an early prefix and restores the basin-conditional and joint stable Gaussian kernel, so the theorem must be synchronized to the corrected class rather than retain its obsolete non-stability conclusion.

changed.from:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
Set \(\Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty)\) and \(V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}\). For any auxiliary finite-support representation \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) almost surely with \(\mathcal J=\{j:P(J=j)>0\}\), set \(p_j=P(J=j)\), \(\Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j)\), \(V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}\), \(\Omega_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}\Omega_j\), and \(V_J=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1\{J=j\}V_j\). These finite-support objects are auxiliary specializations and are not restrictions on the class.
changed.to:
For \(\eta\in\mathsf H\), define
\[
 \Gamma_P(\eta)=E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \frac{g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)g(a,X_t,Y_t(a);\theta^*)^\top}
 {\Pi(a\mid X_t,\eta)}\right].
\]
For every \(j\in\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), set
\[
 p_j=P(J=j),\qquad
 \Omega_j=\Gamma_P(\bar\eta_j),\qquad
 V_j=H^{-1}\Omega_jH^{-\top}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Omega_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}\Omega_j,\qquad
 V_J=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbf1\{J=j\}V_j,
\]
and set
\[
 \Omega_\infty=\Gamma_P(\eta_\infty),\qquad
 V_\infty=H^{-1}\Omega_\infty H^{-\top}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}tail\text{-}selection}\), substitution of \(\eta_\infty=\bar\eta_J\) gives \(\Omega_\infty=\Omega_J\) and \(V_\infty=V_J\) almost surely.
changed.reason: The corrected law class has fixed finite attractors and a class-level terminal label, so the covariance construction must make the basin objects primary rather than optional and must expose the selected-basin equalities.

changed.to: For all distinct \(j,k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(\|\bar\eta_j-\bar\eta_k\|_2\ge s_\eta\).
changed.reason: A positive separation modulus is needed to recover the terminal basin label from the early Cesaro prefix uniformly.

changed.to: For every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(P(J=j)\ge p_-\).
changed.reason: A common positive mass floor is needed for uniform conditioning on every basin.

proposed.statement:
Let \(p\in[1,\infty)\), \(\gamma>0\), and let \((X_i,\mathcal G_i)_{i=1}^n\) be a scalar martingale-difference sequence with \(n\ge2\) and \(\max_i\|X_i\|_\infty\le\gamma\). Put \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2]\), \(V^2=s^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^nE[X_i^2\mid\mathcal G_{i-1}]\), and \(D=\sup_x|P\{s^{-1}\sum_iX_i\le x\}-\Phi(x)|\). There is a constant \(C_{p,\gamma}\) such that
\[
D\le C_{p,\gamma}\left\{\frac{n\log n}{s^3}+\left(\|V^2-1\|_p^p+s^{-2p}\right)^{1/(2p+1)}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1.5. Let p in [1,+infinity) and gamma in (0,+infinity). There exists a constant C_{p,gamma}>0 such that for any n>=2 and any X in M_n satisfying ||X||_infinity<=gamma, D(X)<=C_{p,gamma}[n log(n)/s^3(X)+(||V^2(X)-1||_p^p+s^{-2p}(X))^{1/(2p+1)}]. (1.6)

proposed.name: predictable-QV-growth adaptive IPW-Z class
proposed.construction:
For fixed \(\varepsilon,B,D_1,D_2,h_-,\omega_-,\kappa,s_\Theta,\rho\), fixed compact \(\Theta\), and common deterministic sequences \((r_T,\delta_T)_{T\ge1}\), let \((\mathfrak Q_T)_{T\ge1}\) be any sequence of law classes such that, for every horizon \(T\) and every \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T\), the law \(P\) satisfies
\[
 \mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}full\text{-}data},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:sequential\text{-}randomization},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}overlap},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}score},
\]
\[
 \mathrm{ass:smooth\text{-}z\text{-}map},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}root\text{-}separation},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:root\text{-}interior},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:jacobian\text{-}nonsingular},\quad
 \mathrm{ass:vanishing\text{-}modulus}.
\]
The sequence \((\mathfrak Q_T)_{T\ge1}\), as a whole, is required to satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}predictable\text{-}qv\text{-}growth}\), with the supremum taken over the chosen subclass \(\mathfrak Q_T\) at horizon \(T\). Thus \(\mathfrak Q_T\) is not stipulated to be the maximal class of every law satisfying the pointwise base conditions. In this definition, \(r_T\) and \(\delta_T\) enter only through the numerical approximation tolerance in \(\mathrm{def:ipw\text{-}z\text{-}estimator}\); no state-attraction interpretation is imposed. In particular, membership does not require \(m\), \(J\), \(\eta_\infty\), fixed attractors, attractor separation, basin masses, Cesaro attraction, convergence of \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\), or a terminal covariance.

edit.reason: The predictable-QV condition is uniform over a chosen triangular-array sequence of subclasses; defining the class first as the maximal pointwise base-condition class incorrectly strengthens that collective requirement.

changed.from:
For the predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and the estimator has the uniform linearization
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\]
Without requiring convergence of \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) to any random or deterministic matrix, uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak Q_T\),
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}P(\mathcal E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
\]
so the event truncation is asymptotically inactive uniformly. For the event-truncated sandwich and realized-QV statistic,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T}\sup_{\|c\|_2=1}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) whose basin covariance lower bound is \(\omega_-\) satisfies the predictable-QV growth condition with any strictly smaller positive growth constant. Hence its realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage, including the original truncation threshold \(\omega_-/2\), are corollaries. Saco's Theorem 5.14 is a pointwise realized-QV result for a distinct logged-propensity martingale AIPW/DML setup under variance growth; the two estimator and hypothesis classes are non-nested, and no strict theorem-level tightening is asserted.
changed.to:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\omega_c>0\). For the projected predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\) and \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) need not converge, the contrast-specific truncation is inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The full predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\) satisfies the projected condition simultaneously for all \(\|c\|_2=1\) with the common choice \(\omega_c=\omega_-/(KD_1)^2\). Thus the preceding pivot and coverage conclusions hold with an additional supremum over all unit contrasts on \(\mathfrak Q_T\). Finally, every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies the projected condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\) and every
\[
 0<\omega_c<\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2},
\]
so the same contrast-specific realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage are further corollaries.

changed.from:
Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{k_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference array, \(S_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}\), \(Q_n=\sum_tX_{n,t}^2\), and \(A_n^2=\sum_tE[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]\). If \(A_n^2\to\infty\) in probability, \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\), \(Q_n/A_n^2\to1\) in probability, and for some \(\delta>0\),
\[
 A_n^{-(2+\delta)}\sum_tE[|X_{n,t}|^{2+\delta}]\to0,
\]
then \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).
changed.to:
Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{N_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array, where \(N_n\) and \(h_n\) are deterministic integers satisfying \(0\le h_n<N_n\), and suppose \(|X_{n,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_n\) be a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,h_n}\)-measurable random variable, and let \(\nu_n>0\) be deterministic with \(\lambda_n\ge\nu_n\) almost surely. Define
\[
 S_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t},\qquad
 Q_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t}^2,\qquad
 A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}E[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}].
\]
If
\[
 N_n\nu_n\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 \frac{h_n}{N_n\nu_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{Q_n}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},\qquad
 P(Q_n>0)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
 \frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
All conclusions are uniform over a collection of arrays if \(L\) is common and each displayed convergence premise is uniform over that collection.
changed.reason: The cited floor-only self-normalization claim is false when an early score endogenously selects later variance. The replacement proves the valid early-measurable-scale theorem with a negligible prefix and the information condition \(N_n\nu_n\to\infty\).

Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\omega_c>0\). For the projected predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\) and \(T^{-1}\langle S\rangle_T\) need not converge, the contrast-specific truncation is inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The full predictable-QV-growth class \(\mathfrak Q_T\) satisfies the projected condition simultaneously for all \(\|c\|_2=1\) with the common choice \(\omega_c=\omega_-/(KD_1)^2\). Thus the preceding pivot and coverage conclusions hold with an additional supremum over all unit contrasts on \(\mathfrak Q_T\). Finally, every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies the projected condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\) and every
\[
 0<\omega_c<\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2},
\]
so the same contrast-specific realized-QV pivot and Wald coverage are further corollaries.
changed.to:
Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad
 \omega_{c,T}=\frac{\omega_-\|c\|_2^2}{(KD_1)^2}.
\]
Then \(J_T\) and \(\Lambda_T\) are \(\mathcal F_{k_T}\)-measurable, all early-scale conditions hold uniformly, and the same pivot and coverage conclusions follow.

\[
 S_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t},\qquad
 Q_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t}^2,\qquad
 A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}E[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}].
\]
If
\[
 N_n\nu_n\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 \frac{h_n}{N_n\nu_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{Q_n}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},\qquad
 P(Q_n>0)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
 \frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]

{"id":"thm:uniform-realized-qv-pivot","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix a prespecified \(c\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). For the early-stabilized projected class \(\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)\), the exact-root event is uniformly asymptotically certain and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P(E_T^c)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt T(\widehat\theta_T-\theta^*)+H^{-1}T^{-1/2}S_T
 =O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly. Moreover,
\[
 T^{-1}([S]_T-\langle S\rangle_T)=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat\Omega_T-T^{-1}[S]_T=O_P(T^{-1/2}),\qquad
 \widehat H_T-H=O_P(T^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over that class. Although no information growth is required outside the direction \(H^{-\top}c\), the early-scale condition with \(T\omega_{c,T}\to\infty\) makes the contrast-specific truncation inactive:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}P\{\mathcal E_T(c)^c\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{T_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c)\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak Q_T^{\mathrm{proj}}(c)}
 \left|P\{\tau\in I_T^{\mathrm{rqv}}(c,\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Every finite-tail-attractor class \(\mathfrak P_T\) satisfies this early-stabilized condition for each fixed nonzero \(c\). At every horizon set
\[
 k_T=\min\!\left\{T-1,\left\lceil T\max\{T^{-1/2},\sqrt{r_T}\}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k_T\ge1\), let \(J_T\) be the nearest attractor to \(k_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{k_T}\eta_{t-1}\), with fixed tie-breaking, and set \(J_T=1\) when \(k_T=0\). With \(a=H^{-\top}c\), take
\[
 \Lambda_T=a^\top\Omega_{J_T}a,\qquad

{"id":"lem:saco-self-normalized-martingale-clt","kind":"lemma","statement":"Let \((X_{n,t},\mathcal G_{n,t})_{t=1}^{N_n}\) be a scalar martingale-difference triangular array, where \(N_n\) and \(h_n\) are deterministic integers satisfying \(0\le h_n<N_n\), and suppose \(|X_{n,t}|\le L<\infty\) almost surely. Let \(\lambda_n\) be a positive \(\mathcal G_{n,h_n}\)-measurable random variable, and let \(\nu_n>0\) be deterministic with \(\lambda_n\ge\nu_n\) almost surely. Define
\[
 S_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t},\qquad
 Q_n=\sum_{t=1}^{N_n}X_{n,t}^2,\qquad
 A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}E[X_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}].
\]
If
\[
 N_n\nu_n\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 \frac{h_n}{N_n\nu_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},
\]
then
\[
 \frac{Q_n}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability},\qquad
 P(Q_n>0)\longrightarrow1,\qquad
 \frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
All conclusions are uniform over a collection of arrays if \(L\) is common and each displayed convergence premise is uniform over that collection.","free_symbols":[],"depends_on":[],"status":"proved","proof_tex":"Put \(b_n^2=N_n\lambda_n\).  For \(t>h_n\), define
\[
 Y_{n,t}=X_{n,t}/b_n,qquad
 v_{n,t}=E[Y_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}],qquad
 V_n=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}v_{n,t}.
\tag{1}
\]
Division is legal because \(\lambda_n\ge\nu_n>0\).  Since \(b_n\) is \(\mathcal G_{n,h_n}\)-measurable, it is \(\mathcal G_{n,t-1}\)-measurable for \(t>h_n\); hence the suffix is again a martingale-difference array.  The increment bound and the first and third hypotheses give
\[
 \max_{t>h_n}|Y_{n,t}|
 \le\epsilon_n:=\frac{L}{\sqrt{N_n\nu_n}}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad V_n=\frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
\tag{2}
\]
in probability.

Retain the increment at time \(t>h_n\) only when \(\sum_{s=h_n+1}^{t-1}v_{n,s}\le2\).  This indicator is predictable.  Denote the retained increment and variance by \(\widetilde Y_{n,t}\) and \(\widetilde v_{n,t}\).  Then
\[
 \sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}\widetilde v_{n,t}\le2+\epsilon_n^2.
\tag{3}
\]
For fixed \(u\in\mathbb R\), Taylor's formula and the martingale-difference property imply
\[
 E[e^{iu\widetilde Y_{n,t}}\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]
 =1-\frac{u^2}{2}\widetilde v_{n,t}+r_{n,t},
 \qquad |r_{n,t}|\le\frac{|u|^3}{6}\epsilon_n\widetilde v_{n,t}.
\tag{4}
\]
Define
\[
 Z_{n,j}=\exp\!\left\{iu\sum_{t=h_n+1}^j\widetilde Y_{n,t}
 +\frac{u^2}{2}\sum_{t=h_n+1}^j\widetilde v_{n,t}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Using (4) and \(|e^x-1-x|\le x^2e^x/2\) for \(x\ge0\), conditional expectation gives
\[
 \left|E[Z_{n,j}\mid\mathcal G_{n,j-1}]-Z_{n,j-1}\right|
 \le C_u e^{u^2(2+\epsilon_n^2)/2}
 \left(\epsilon_n\widetilde v_{n,j}+\widetilde v_{n,j}^2\right).
\tag{6}
\]
Since \(\widetilde v_{n,j}\le\epsilon_n^2\), summing (6) and using (3) gives \(E[Z_{n,N_n}]\to1\).  By (2), stopping changes the suffix only on \(\{V_n>2\}\), whose probability tends to zero.  The stopped total variance \(\widetilde V_n=\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}\widetilde v_{n,t}\) converges in probability to one and is bounded by \(2+\epsilon_n^2\), so
\[
 E\left|1-\exp\{u^2(\widetilde V_n-1)/2\}\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
The identity
\[
 e^{-u^2/2}Z_{n,N_n}
 =e^{iu\sum_t\widetilde Y_{n,t}}
 e^{u^2(\widetilde V_n-1)/2}
\]
together with (6)--(7), followed by removal of \(\{V_n>2\}\), shows that the suffix characteristic function converges to \(e^{-u^2/2}\) for every \(u\).  The characteristic-function continuity criterion gives
\[
 \sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}X_{n,t}/b_n\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{8}
\]

The prefix is negligible on this scale.  Martingale orthogonality and boundedness give
\[
 E\left(\sum_{t=1}^{h_n}X_{n,t}\right)^2
 =\sum_{t=1}^{h_n}E[X_{n,t}^2]\le h_nL^2.
\tag{9}
\]
Since \(b_n^2\ge N_n\nu_n\), Chebyshev's inequality and the second hypothesis yield
\[
 b_n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{h_n}X_{n,t}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (8)--(10) prove \(S_n/b_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

For realized quadratic variation put \(D_{n,t}=Y_{n,t}^2-v_{n,t}\) for \(t>h_n\).  These are martingale differences and
\[
 E[D_{n,t}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]
 \le E[Y_{n,t}^4\mid\mathcal G_{n,t-1}]
 \le\epsilon_n^2v_{n,t}.
\tag{11}
\]
Under the same predictable stopping rule, martingale orthogonality bounds the second moment of the stopped sum by \(\epsilon_n^2(2+\epsilon_n^2)\).  Removing \(\{V_n>2\}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}D_{n,t}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{12}
\]
The prefix squares satisfy
\[
 0\le b_n^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{h_n}X_{n,t}^2
 \le\frac{h_nL^2}{N_n\nu_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{Q_n}{b_n^2}
 =b_n^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{h_n}X_{n,t}^2+V_n
 +\sum_{t=h_n+1}^{N_n}D_{n,t}
 \longrightarrow1
\tag{14}
\]
in probability.  Hence \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\).  On \(\{Q_n/b_n^2\in[1/2,3/2]\}\), division is legal, and (8)--(10), (14), and continuity of \(x\mapsto x^{-1/2}\) give
\[
 \frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}
 =\frac{S_n/b_n}{\sqrt{Q_n/b_n^2}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{15}
\]
Every bound depends only on the common \(L\) and the three displayed premise errors.  Applying the argument to any contrary sequence of member arrays proves all asserted uniform conclusions."}

{"id":"def:saco-early-stabilized-aipw-class","name":"Saco enumerated AIPW class with early QV stabilization","construction":"For each row \(n\), let \(\mathcal T_n=\{t_{n,1}<\cdots<t_{n,N_n}\}\) be a deterministic scored set, fixed before data collection, and put \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}=|\mathcal T_n|\).  The class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}=(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}})_{n\ge1}\) consists of triangular arrays of binary-treatment laws with the following properties, imposed row by row and uniformly over the displayed class.

First, the source conditions retained from Saco are written out explicitly.  For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(Y_{n,t}(a)\) is the potential outcome depending only on the current treatment, and \(Y_{n,t}=A_{n,t}Y_{n,t}(1)+(1-A_{n,t})Y_{n,t}(0)\) almost surely.  The triples \((X_{n,t},Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\) are independent and identically distributed over \(t\) within a row and are unaffected by the adaptive policy.  There is a pre-treatment sigma-field \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), containing the past and \(X_{n,t}\), such that the logged propensity \(\pi_{n,t}\) is \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\)-measurable and
\[
0<\pi_{n,t}<1,\qquad
\mathbb P_n(A_{n,t}=1\mid\mathcal B_{n,t})=\pi_{n,t}\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal B_{n,t}\), \(A_{n,t}\) is independent of \((Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1))\).  There is one constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) such that
\[
\epsilon\le\pi_{n,t}\le1-\epsilon
\quad\text{almost surely for every }t\in\mathcal T_n.
\]
For each \(a\), the fitted regression \(\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}\), as a random function, is measurable with respect to the history \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\).  There are finite constants \(C_Y,C_M\), common to the class, such that
\[
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t,a}E_{\mathbb P_n}|Y_{n,t}(a)|^4\le C_Y,\qquad
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,t\in\mathcal T_n,a}
E_{\mathbb P_n}|\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}(X_{n,t})|^4\le C_M.
\]
Thus these are uniform versions of source Assumptions \(3.5,3.6,3.2,3.7,3.8,4.5,4.8,3.9,\) and \(3.10\), in the order specified by the directive.

Define the causal target, AIPW pseudo-outcome, centered score, estimator, and its sample variance by
\[
\theta_{0,n}=E_{\mathbb P_n}\{Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)\},
\]
\[
\widehat\phi_{n,t}=\frac{A_{n,t}}{\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})\}
-\frac{1-A_{n,t}}{1-\pi_{n,t}}
\{Y_{n,t}-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t})\}
+\widehat m_{n,t-1,1}(X_{n,t})-\widehat m_{n,t-1,0}(X_{n,t}),
\]
\[
X_{n,s}=\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\theta_{0,n},\qquad
S_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s},\qquad
Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}X_{n,s}^2,
\]
\[
\widehat\theta_n=N_n^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}},\qquad
\widehat V_n=(N_n-1)^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}
\{\widehat\phi_{n,t_{n,s}}-\widehat\theta_n\}^2
\quad(N_n\ge2).
\]
To order the deterministic scored set without discarding interstitial history, define
\[
\mathcal G_{n,0}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,1}-1},\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,s}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s+1}-1}\ (1\le s<N_n),\qquad
\mathcal G_{n,N_n}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,N_n}}.
\]
Then \(X_{n,s}\) is \(\mathcal G_{n,s}\)-measurable and \(\mathcal G_{n,s-1}=\mathcal F_{n,t_{n,s}-1}\).  Put
\[
V_n^2=\sum_{s=1}^{N_n}E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}].
\]
The source variance-growth Assumption \(5.11\) is retained: \(N_n\to\infty\), and for one \(v_->0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n(V_n^2<v_-N_n)\longrightarrow0.
\]

\[
\frac{k_n}{N_n}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \Lambda_n\ge\lambda_-\quad\text{almost surely},
\]

\[
A_{n,+}^2=\sum_{s=k_n+1}^{N_n}
E_{\mathbb P_n}[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}],

\]

Under the binary recoding in which Saco's treatment indicator is one for the present arm \(1\) and zero for the present arm \(2\), the bounded two-regime experiment constructed in the preceding proposition satisfies every assumption explicitly listed in Saco's Theorem 5.14 and also its maintained consistency and no-interference condition. Indeed, take the deterministic scored set to be all \(T\) occasions, take both predictable nuisance regressions to be identically zero, take \(Y_t(0)=Y_t(1)=1\) in Saco's binary notation, and take his target to be \(\theta_0=0=\theta^*\). His centered AIPW increment is then exactly \(\xi_t\), and his realized and predictable quadratic variations are \(Q_T=[S]_T\) and \(V_T^2=\langle S\rangle_T\), with \(V_T^2\ge 4T\) almost surely. Nevertheless, along \(T=2n\),
\[
 \frac{S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Longrightarrow
 \mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and the displayed limit has nonzero mean. The feasible sample-variance Studentized AIPW statistic has the same limit. Therefore the variance-growth-only Studentized central limit conclusion asserted in Saco's Theorem 5.14 is false as stated.

Under the binary recoding in which Saco's treatment indicator is one for the present arm \(1\) and zero for the present arm \(2\), the bounded two-regime experiment constructed in the preceding proposition satisfies every assumption explicitly listed in Saco's Theorem 5.14 and also its maintained consistency and no-interference condition. Indeed, take the deterministic scored set to be all \(T\) occasions, take both predictable nuisance regressions to be identically zero, take \(Y_t(0)=Y_t(1)=1\) in Saco's binary notation, and take his target to be \(\theta_0=0=\theta^*\). His centered AIPW increment is then exactly \(\xi_t\); conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), the observable centered score has the nondegenerate two-point law \(P(\xi_t=1/p_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=p_t\) and \(P(\xi_t=-1/(1-p_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1-p_t\); hence \(E(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1/p_t+1/(1-p_t)\in\{4,16/3\}\), and his realized and predictable quadratic variations are \(Q_T=[S]_T\) and \(V_T^2=\langle S\rangle_T\), with \(V_T^2\ge 4T\) almost surely. Nevertheless, along \(T=2n\),
\[
 \frac{S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Longrightarrow
 \mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and the displayed limit has nonzero mean. The feasible sample-variance Studentized AIPW statistic has the same limit. Therefore the variance-growth-only Studentized central limit conclusion asserted in Saco's Theorem 5.14 is false as stated.

At every even horizon \(T=2n\), the bounded two-regime score and randomization process of Proposition~\(\text{prop:endogenous-qv-self-normalization-obstruction}\) has an explicit bounded augmentation with a nondegenerate observable-outcome law and a nonzero causal effect that satisfies every assumption explicitly listed in Saco's Theorem~5.14 and also its maintained consistency and no-interference condition. Namely, let \((U_t)_{t=1}^T\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the action randomizers, set \(A_t^{\mathrm S}:=\mathbf1\{A_t=1\}\) and \(X_t^{\mathrm S}:=(X_t,U_t)\), and set
\[
 Y_t^{\mathrm S}(1)=\frac32+U_t,
 \qquad
 Y_t^{\mathrm S}(0)=\frac12+U_t.
\]
At context value \((x,u)\), set the predictable nuisance regressions to \(\widehat m_{t-1,1}(x,u)=u+1/2\) and \(\widehat m_{t-1,0}(x,u)=u-1/2\). Then the causal target is \(\theta_0=E_P[Y_t^{\mathrm S}(1)-Y_t^{\mathrm S}(0)]=1\), while the observed outcome obeys \(\operatorname{Var}(Y_t^{\mathrm S}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1+p_t(1-p_t)\ge1\), where \(p_t:=P(A_t=1\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\). Saco's centered AIPW increment is nevertheless exactly \(\xi_t\). Conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\),
\[
 P\!\left(\xi_t=\frac1{p_t}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right)=p_t,
 \qquad
 P\!\left(\xi_t=-\frac1{1-p_t}\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_{t-1}\right)=1-p_t,
\]
and hence \(E(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=1/p_t+1/(1-p_t)\in\{4,16/3\}\). Saco's realized and predictable quadratic variations are therefore \(Q_T=[S]_T\) and \(V_T^2=\langle S\rangle_T\), with \(V_T^2\ge4T\) almost surely. Nevertheless, along \(T=2n\),
\[
 \frac{S_T}{\sqrt{Q_T}}\Longrightarrow
 L:=\mathbf1\{Z>0\}\frac{2Z+4W/\sqrt3}{\sqrt{28/3}}
 +\mathbf1\{Z\le0\}\frac{2Z+2W}{\sqrt8},
\]
where \(Z,W\) are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and
\[
 E[L]=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac3{28}}-\frac1{\sqrt8}\right)\ne0.
\]
The feasible sample-variance Studentized AIPW statistic has the same limit \(L\). Thus the variance-growth-only normal-limit conclusions asserted in Saco's Theorem~5.14 are false as stated, even for bounded nondegenerate outcomes and a nonzero causal effect.

{"id":"thm:saco-early-stabilized-aipw-pivot","kind":"theorem","statement":"For the class in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}class}\), let \(S_n,Q_n,\widehat\theta_n,\widehat V_n,\theta_{0,n}\), and \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}\) have the meanings given there.  Then the centered AIPW scores are martingale differences in deterministic scored-set order, and there is a finite constant \(C_X\), depending only on the common overlap and outcome/nuisance fourth-moment envelopes, such that
\[
\sup_{n,\mathbb P_n,s}E_{\mathbb P_n}|X_{n,s}|^4\le C_X.
\]
For every \(\zeta>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\mathbb P_n\left(\left|\frac{Q_n}{N_n\Lambda_n}-1\right|>\zeta\right)\longrightarrow0,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
\left|\mathbb P_n\left\{\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\le z\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
where the score ratio is set to zero when \(Q_n=0\).  If
\[
Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{N_n}(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{0,n})/\sqrt{\widehat V_n},&\widehat V_n>0,\\
0,&\widehat V_n=0,
\end{cases}
\]
then
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
\left|\mathbb P_n\{Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}\le z\}-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the interval
\[
\mathcal I_n(\alpha)=\left[\widehat\theta_n\ \pm\ \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{\widehat V_n/N_n}\right]
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_n\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{Saco,es}}}
\left|\mathbb P_n\{\theta_{0,n}\in\mathcal I_n(\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the valid direct repair is Saco's published enumerated AIPW/DML class intersected with early measurable suffix-QV stabilization, not the variance-growth-only source class.","free_symbols":["\alpha","\Phi"],"depends_on":["def:saco-early-stabilized-aipw-class","lem:early-measurable-l4-self-normalized-martingale-clt","lem:saco-pointwise-rqv-pivot"],"status":"proved","justification":"This is the direct theorem for Saco's enumerated AIPW/DML setup: it derives the fourth-moment score control and proves uniform realized-QV, feasible Studentized, and Wald limits on the early-stabilized intersection class.","gap":"Saco's variance-growth-only conclusion is refuted by the existing in-class two-regime witness; the theorem identifies and proves the sufficient early-information repair without importing bounded generic scores.","consumer":"A HeartSteps-style causal excursion analysis using predictable AIPW nuisances can use the feasible sample-variance interval once the scored suffix has an early-measurable information scale.","proof_tex":"Fix one row and abbreviate \(t=t_{n,s}\), \(\pi=\pi_{n,t}\), and \(M_a=\widehat m_{n,t-1,a}(X_{n,t})\).  Conditional on the past, the current covariate, and the two current potential outcomes, logging integrity, conditional treatment independence, and consistency from Definition~\(\mathrm{def:saco\text{-}early\text{-}stabilized\text{-}aipw\text{-}class}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E[\widehat\phi_{n,t}\mid\mathcal B_{n,t},Y_{n,t}(0),Y_{n,t}(1)]
&=(Y_{n,t}(1)-M_1)-(Y_{n,t}(0)-M_0)+M_1-M_0\\
&=Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
The current full-data triple is independent of the past and identically distributed within the row.  Taking conditional expectation of (1) given \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\) therefore yields
\[
E[\widehat\phi_{n,t}-\theta_{0,n}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1}]=0.
\tag{2}
\]
By the scored-order filtration in the definition, \(\mathcal G_{n,s-1}=\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\).  Hence (2) proves
\[
E[X_{n,s}\mid\mathcal G_{n,s-1}]=0.
\tag{3}
\]
This establishes the martingale-difference property in scored-set order; it does not treat the scored observations as independent.

We next derive, rather than assume, the fourth-moment envelope needed for the martingale argument.  Uniform overlap implies the pathwise bound
\[
|\widehat\phi_{n,t}|\le(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\{|Y_{n,t}(0)|+|Y_{n,t}(1)|+|M_0|+|M_1|\}.
\tag{4}
\]
For nonnegative \(u_1,\ldots,u_r\), convexity gives \((\sum_{j=1}^ru_j)^4\le r^3\sum_{j=1}^ru_j^4\).  Hence (4) and the two uniform source envelopes give
\[
E|\widehat\phi_{n,t}|^4
\le64(1+\epsilon^{-1})^4(2C_Y+2C_M).
\tag{5}
\]
Jensen's inequality and \(|x-y|^4\le8(|x|^4+|y|^4)\) also give
\[
|\theta_{0,n}|^4
\le E|Y_{n,t}(1)-Y_{n,t}(0)|^4\le16C_Y.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (5)--(6),
\[
E|X_{n,s}|^4
\le C_X:=512(1+\epsilon^{-1})^4(2C_Y+2C_M)+128C_Y<\infty.
\tag{7}
\]
Every constant is common to the triangular-array class.  This is the required transfer from Saco's outcome and nuisance assumptions to the AIPW score; no bounded-increment premise has been introduced.

Apply Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:early\text{-}measurable\text{-}l4\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}martingale\text{-}clt}\) with \(h_n=k_n\), \(\lambda_n=\Lambda_n\), and \(N_n=n_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  Equation (3) supplies the martingale premise, (7) supplies its fourth-moment premise, and the class definition supplies \(k_n/N_n\to0\), \(\Lambda_n\ge\lambda_->0\), and
\[
\frac{A_{n,+}^2}{N_n\Lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
\tag{8}
\]
uniformly.  The lemma therefore proves both
\[
\frac{Q_n}{N_n\Lambda_n}\longrightarrow1
\tag{9}
\]
in probability and the asserted uniform standard-normal limit for \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}\).  In particular \(P(Q_n>0)\to1\) uniformly.  Notice that (8) and \(\Lambda_n\ge\lambda_-\) also imply the retained source variance-growth condition with any fixed \(v_-<\lambda_-\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), but that numbered source condition was retained explicitly in the class rather than silently discarded.

It remains to pass from realized QV to Saco's feasible sample variance.  The definitions give the exact identities
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{0,n}=\frac{S_n}{N_n},\qquad
(N_n-1)\widehat V_n=Q_n-\frac{S_n^2}{N_n}.
\tag{10}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz ensures \(0\le S_n^2\le N_nQ_n\).  The score-pivot limit implies \(S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}=O_P(1)\) uniformly, so on \(\{Q_n>0\}\),
\[
\frac{N_n\widehat V_n}{Q_n}
=\frac{N_n}{N_n-1}\left\{1-\frac1{N_n}\left(\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{Q_n}}\right)^2\right\}\longrightarrow1
\tag{11}
\]
in probability, uniformly.  Equations (9) and (11) imply \(P(\widehat V_n>0)\to1\).  On that event, (10)--(11) give
\[
Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}
=\frac{S_n/\sqrt{Q_n}}{\sqrt{N_n\widehat V_n/Q_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
\tag{12}
\]
uniformly.  Continuity of the standard normal distribution function upgrades (12) to the displayed uniform Kolmogorov conclusion.

Finally, with \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), the event \(\{\theta_{0,n}\in\mathcal I_n(\alpha)\}\) agrees on \(\{\widehat V_n>0\}\) with \(\{|Z_n^{\mathrm{feas}}|\le z_\alpha\}\).  The exceptional event has probability tending uniformly to zero, and the normal limit has
\[
\Phi(z_\alpha)-\Phi(-z_\alpha)=1-\alpha.
\tag{13}
\]
The uniform distributional convergence in (12) and (13) prove the asserted Wald coverage.  Saco's ten numbered source conditions, Assumptions~3.5, 3.6, 3.2, 3.7, 3.8, 4.5, 4.8, 3.9, 3.10, and 5.11, are recorded explicitly in the preceding class definition.  The extra premise used above is precisely (8), so the theorem's class is their intersection with early QV stabilization, as claimed."}

changed.to:
Write \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t=(\beta_1,\beta_2,q_1,q_2)^\top\) for the current augmented state. Its induced armwise update is
\[
q_a^+=\frac{q_a}{1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2},\qquad
\beta_a^+=\frac{\beta_a+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aXY(a)}{1+\mathbf 1\{A=a\}q_aX^2}.
\]
The next clipped-UCB action uses \(\beta_aX+|X|\sqrt{q_a}\), so \(Z^{\mathrm{GX}}_t\), rather than its two-dimensional slope projection, is the time-homogeneous Markov state. Put \(D_{t,a}=\Phi^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(N_{t,a}=b^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,a}\), \(C_{t,a}=\mathbf 1\{A_t=a\}\), and, for \(t\geq1\),
\[
\Psi_t=\left(\frac{D_{t,1}}t,\frac{D_{t,2}}t,\frac{N_{t,1}}t,\frac{N_{t,2}}t\right),\qquad
U_{t+1}=\bigl(C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}^2,C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}^2,
C_{t+1,1}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(1),C_{t+1,2}X_{t+1}Y_{t+1}(2)\bigr).
\]
With \(\gamma_t=1/t\), the sufficient-statistic updates give the exact recursion
\[
\Psi_{t+1}-\Psi_t=\gamma_{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t)=\frac1{t+1}(U_{t+1}-\Psi_t).
\]

Here is the actual one-step finite expectation under the bounded law in Definition~\(\textnormal{def:guoxu-recursion}\). Let \(\mu_1=1/2\), \(\mu_2=1/12\), let \(p_{t,1}(1)=u_t\), \(p_{t,1}(-4)=v_t\), and let \(p_{t,2}(x)=1-p_{t,1}(x)\). Conditional on \(\mathcal F_t\), independence and equiprobability of \(X_{t+1}\) and the innovations \(R_{t+1,a}\) give the finite law
\[
\operatorname{guoXuNoiseLaw}_t(x,a,r_1,r_2)
=\frac18p_{t,a}(x),
\quad x\in\{-4,1\},\quad a\in\{1,2\},\quad r_1,r_2\in\{-1,1\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal U(x,a,r_1,r_2)=
\bigl(\mathbf1\{a=1\}x^2,\mathbf1\{a=2\}x^2,
\mathbf1\{a=1\}x(\mu_1+\sigma_1r_1),
\mathbf1\{a=2\}x(\mu_2+\sigma_2r_2)\bigr).
\]
Thus the conditional expectation is the displayed finite sum
\[
E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]
=\sum_{x\in\{-4,1\}}\sum_{a=1}^2\sum_{r_1,r_2\in\{-1,1\}}
\operatorname{guoXuNoiseLaw}_t(x,a,r_1,r_2)\mathcal U(x,a,r_1,r_2)
=h(u_t,v_t),
\]
where
\[
h(u,v)=\left(\frac{u+16v}{2},\frac{17-u-16v}{2},
\frac{u-4v}{4},\frac{-3-u+4v}{24}\right).
\]
Let
\[
M_{t+1}=U_{t+1}-E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t],
\qquad
R_{j,k}=\sum_{s=j}^k\gamma_{s+1}M_{s+1}\quad(j\leq k).
\]
For every coordinate \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\), every \(\epsilon>0\), and every initialized law \(P_{\eta_0}\), the coordinatewise dyadic tail estimate proved in equation (12) is
\[
P_{\eta_0}\!\left\{\exists\ell\geq L:\ 
\sup_{k\geq2^\ell}\left|R_{2^\ell,k}^{(i)}\right|>\epsilon\right\}
\leq \frac{C_i}{\epsilon^2}\sum_{\ell\geq L}2^{-\ell}
\longrightarrow0\qquad(L\to\infty),
\]
for a finite constant \(C_i\) depending only on the fixed bounded-noise envelope.

For \(C<\infty\) and \(c>0\), define the compact carrier
\[
\mathsf K(C,c)=[c,C]^2\times[-C,C]^2.
\]
For the recursion above one may take
\[
c_{\mathrm{GX}}=\frac{17}{400},\qquad
C_{\mathrm{GX}}=\max\left\{17,1+4\max\left\{\frac12+\sigma_1,\frac1{12}+\sigma_2\right\}\right\};
\]
then \(\Psi_t\in\mathsf K(C_{\mathrm{GX}},c_{\mathrm{GX}})\) eventually almost surely. Put \(p=99/100\), \(q=1/100\), \(h_+=h(p,q)\), \(h_-=h(q,p)\), \(h_1=h(p,p)\), \(h_2=h(q,q)\), and, for \(\psi=(d_1,d_2,n_1,n_2)\in\mathsf K(C,c)\), put \(\Delta(\psi)=n_1/d_1-n_2/d_2\). The exact four-mode convexified graph on this carrier is
\[
F_{C,c}(\psi)=
\begin{cases}
\{h_+-\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)>0,\\
\{h_--\psi\},&\Delta(\psi)<0,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1<d_2,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1>d_2,\\
\operatorname{co}\{h_+,h_-,h_1,h_2\}-\psi,&\Delta(\psi)=0,\ d_1=d_2.
\end{cases}
\]
Its graph is understood in the relative topology of \(\mathsf K(C,c)\times\mathbb R^4\); it is relatively closed there and has nonempty compact convex values. No ambient closed-graph assertion at the boundary of \(\{d_1,d_2>0\}\) is part of this handle. The name \(\operatorname{GuoXuReductionConditions}(C,c)\) denotes only: the exact recursion above; eventual containment in \(\mathsf K(C,c)\); the relative closed-graph and compact-convex-value properties just stated; the switching-layer drift inclusion
\[
E[U_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]-\Psi_t\in F_{C,c}^{\,c_0t^{-1/2}}(\Psi_t)
\]
for some finite deterministic \(c_0\) and all sufficiently large \(t\); boundedness of \(U_{t+1}\) and \(\Psi_t\); and the displayed coordinatewise dyadic tail limit for \(R_{j,k}\).

For clarity, the compact-initial-set finite-attractor property is only a named target for future work. For \(m_{\mathrm{GX}}\geq1\), distinct deterministic targets \(\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_1,\ldots,\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}\in\mathbb R^2\), and a \(\sigma(\bigcup_{t\geq1}\mathcal F_t)\)-measurable selector \(J_{\mathrm{GX}}\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\mathrm{GX}}\}\), define
\[
B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j=\{\eta_0\in\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}:P_{\eta_0}(J_{\mathrm{GX}}=j)>0\},
\qquad
\mathcal L_{\eta_0}=\left\{\lim_{t\to\infty}
(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
=\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\right\}.
\]
For a compact set
\[
K_0\subset\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_{\mathrm{GX}}}
\operatorname{relint}_{\mathsf K_{\mathrm{GX}}}(B^{\mathrm{GX}}_j),
\]
define the event
\[
\mathcal A_T(\eta_0,K_0)=\left\{
\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T
\left\|(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,1},\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{t,2})^\top
-\bar\beta^{\mathrm{GX}}_{J_{\mathrm{GX}}}\right\|_2
\leq r_T(K_0)\right\}.
\]
For nonnegative deterministic sequences \(r_T(K_0)\) and \(\delta_T(K_0)\), the future predicate \(\operatorname{CompactAttraction}_{\mathrm{GX}}(K_0)\) means
\[
P_{\eta_0}(\mathcal L_{\eta_0})=1\quad\text{for every }\eta_0\in K_0,
\qquad
\sup_{\eta_0\in K_0}P_{\eta_0}\{\mathcal A_T(\eta_0,K_0)^c\}
\leq\delta_T(K_0),
\qquad
r_T(K_0)\to0,\quad\delta_T(K_0)\to0.
\]
This future predicate is not asserted by this definition or by the present dynamics theorem, and it is not a conjunct of \(\operatorname{GuoXuReductionConditions}(C,c)\). In particular, the handle posits neither a quantitative-hitting condition, nor a quantitative-escape condition, nor an arbitrary auxiliary vanishing sequence.
changed.reason: The current handle omits the one-step finite law and equation-(12) martingale objects, states graph closure without an explicit compact carrier, and phrases unproved compact-uniform attraction as positive method-specific obligations. The corrected construction records the exact recursion and expectation, restricts the four-mode graph to its eventual compact carrier, and separates the unasserted finite-attractor/Cesaro target from the reduction conditions.
